slope-negative.question: What is the slope of the tangent line to $y=x^2$ at $x=-1.5$?
slope-negative.explanation: The derivative is $f'(x)=2x$, so $f'(-1.5)=-3$. The slope is negative because the parabola is going down on the left of its lowest point. In the picture the secant slope $2a+h$ gets close to $2a=-3$ as $h$ shrinks.

corner.question: Does the graph of $y=|x|$ have a tangent line at $x=0$?
options: No: the slope from the left is $-1$ and from the right is $1$
corner.explanation: To the right of 0, $|x|=x$ has slope 1. To the left, $|x|=-x$ has slope $-1$. The secant slopes from the two sides do not head to the same number, so $f'(0)$ does not exist: the graph has a corner there.
